title: Unravel
notes: Steam copy, launched from Highball through Steam → EA app (EASteamLauncher). It launches, renders through DXVK (1280x800 swapchain) and plays. I checked it for a few minutes, with no frame rate measured. The protection is EA OOA 4.10.0.680 (`Core\Activation64.dll`, plus a 32-bit `Core\ActivationUI.exe`). **Workaround and why.** On the arm64 line FEX gives a 32-bit (WoW64) process a CPU without AVX, FMA, F16C, XSAVE, AVX2 or BMI1/2, while a 64-bit (ARM64EC) process gets one with them (FEX-Emu/FEX#5993). The x64 EA app fetches a license bound to the CPU it sees. The 32-bit ActivationUI then sees a different CPU, deletes the `.dlf` and falls back to its login dialog, which can't reach EA ("invalid email or password", "computer is currently offline"). `FEX_HOSTFEATURES=disableavx` makes both sides report the same CPUID. It has to reach the EA app too, not just the game. The CPUID tables and traces are in the comments below. **x64 engines (x64-crossover26.3-r31, Rosetta): does not launch.** The license is fine (`License signature is good`), but `Unravel.exe` relaunches itself `/dbrv=1..5` about every 10 s and quits with 0xFFFFFFFA. Right before each relaunch the log has `NtSetContextThread Setting debug registers is not supported under Rosetta, faking success`. This is the same symptom as Need for Speed 2015 in MathiasKowoll/MacGameFix#134. It doesn't change with HB_X87SIDECAR unset or with the EA overlay removed. **Setup snag on both engines.** When Steam's install script installs the EA app (rather than the ea-app recipe), `Program Files\Electronic Arts\EA Desktop\EA Desktop` is left as the empty `EA Desktop?` stub. I replaced it by hand with a symlink to `13.827.2.6342/EA Desktop`, and also moved IGO64/IGO32 out of the way. Edited after the fix. The original report said "1 — does not launch"; the investigation is in the comments.
issues: Needs FEX_HOSTFEATURES=disableavx on the arm64 engine, or EA OOA rejects its license and shows a dead login dialog. Does not launch at all on x64 engines (debug registers under Rosetta).
